slides.say: A school has two buses. Bus A carries four times as many students as bus B. Six students move from bus A to bus B. Afterwards, bus B carries half as many students as bus A. How many students are on the two buses altogether?

Students move from one bus to the other, and the ratio changes. We'll solve it two ways, the math way with an equation, and then by understanding, with divisibility, which needs almost no calculation.

Let's start with the math way. Bus A carries four times as many as bus B. Remember, the plain x goes to the smaller one. B is the smaller bus, so B is x and A is four x. No fractions, and no dividing later.
at: so B is x and A is four x

slides.say: Six students move from A to B. A loses six, so A has four x minus six. B gains six, so B has x plus six.
Afterwards, B carries half as many as A. So B is the little guy, and it gets the times two. Two times B is equal to A. Two times x plus six is equal to four x minus six.

Now we open the brackets. So two x plus twelve is equal to four x minus six. We take two x from both sides, and add six to both sides. Twelve plus six is eighteen, so eighteen is two x, and x is nine.

Careful, don't mark nine. That's bus B at the start, and they ask about both buses together. Moving students doesn't change the total, so the total is x plus four x, five x. Five times nine is forty-five. Choice number two is our answer.
at: so the total is x plus four x
Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now by understanding. We start again from the givens. At the start, A has four times B. So for every one student on B, there are four on A. One part and four parts, five parts in all. So the total divides by five.
Forty-eight doesn't divide by five, so choice number three is out.
After the move, B has half of A. One part and two parts, three parts in all. And the total didn't change, because the students only moved. So the total also divides by three.

Forty is thirty-nine plus one. And thirty-nine is three times thirteen. So forty doesn't divide by three. Fifty is forty-eight plus two. And forty-eight is three times sixteen. So fifty doesn't either. Choice numbers one and four are out.

Only forty-five is left, and it divides by both. Forty-five is five times nine. It's also three times fifteen. So when a total is split in a ratio, it divides by the sum of the ratio numbers, before and after. Choice number two is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
